clue.text: Minor road accident in 9 as guitar man turned left

parts.note: a Fender is the American electric guitar, as in the Stratocaster
Ben is a man's name

indicators.note: turned says the word for left is read backwards

parts.note: red means left-wing in politics

explanation.surface: A guitarist swerves left and has a small prang, as reported from New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in 9' points to the answer at 9-across, New York: the phrase is American usage. 'turned' reverses RED to DER.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang for a small collision that dents a car's wings, which Americans call fenders.

clue.text: Pro mounted a chimney in compound

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means the words read upwards

parts.note: lum is a Scots and northern word for a chimney

explanation.surface: A professional climbs a chimney inside some industrial compound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted' reverses upward in a down clue, giving MULA. 'compound' looks like an enclosure but is the chemist's mixture; LUM is Scots for chimney.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical formula names the make-up of a compound, so the two stand for each other.

clue.text: Calcium lacking in pet food

indicators.note: lacking says a piece is missing from the word

parts.note: to pet is to kiss and cuddle, to canoodle
Ca is the chemical symbol for calcium

explanation.surface: Some brand of pet food is short of calcium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pet food' reads as one thing; 'pet' is a verb meaning canoodle, and 'food' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodles are a pasta-like foodstuff, so a single one is an item of food.

clue.text: Regular Tuesday meeting with associate at the end of the day

definitions.text: at the end of the day

parts.note: regular means steady or level, even
an associate or partner is an ally

explanation.surface: A weekly Tuesday meeting with a colleague held at close of business.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms meaning finally, in the long run, after all is done.

clue.text: Car designer, solvent, but short of pennies occasionally

indicators.note: short of means lacking certain letters

parts.note: benzene is a common industrial solvent

indicators.note: occasionally picks every other letter of the word pennies

explanation.surface: A car designer who is solvent yet sometimes short of a penny or two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes ENE from 'pennies' (its 2nd, 4th and 6th letters), and 'short of' removes it from BENZENE. 'solvent' looks like 'in funds' but is the chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: Karl Benz built the first practical motor car, giving his name to Mercedes-Benz.

clue.text: It's impossible to protect a daughter and son in these times

indicators.note: to protect is to surround and shield, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: no way is a flat refusal, saying a thing cannot happen
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent laments that it is impossible to keep children safe in the modern world.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean at the present time, in the current era.

clue.text: Head of employment has reason to be touchy …

indicators.note: head of picks the opening letter of the word employment

parts.note: a reason for acting is a motive

explanation.surface: A head of HR has good reason to be sensitive about something.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue into 7-down's surface; it plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A touchy subject is a sensitive, feeling-charged one, likely to stir strong reactions.

clue.text: … in relation to new nepotistic position in office

parts.note: re means concerning, in relation to

indicators.note: new suggests the letters of nepotistic are made into something fresh

explanation.surface: Continuing 6-down: the boss is touchy about a new job given through nepotism.
explanation.definitionFit: The front-desk worker greeting visitors holds a job, a post, in an office.

clue.text: Nobleman with award finds place to hang decoration

parts.note: an earl is a British nobleman
the OBE (Order of the British Empire) is a British honour

explanation.surface: A peer who wins an honour looks for somewhere to hang the medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decoration' suggests the medal; here it is an earring.
explanation.definitionFit: Earrings are ornaments worn hanging from the soft lower part of the ear.

clue.text: City briefly featuring in Bunyan and Tennyson

definitions.text: City briefly featuring in Bunyan and Tennyson

parts.words: City briefly featuring in Bunyan and Tennyson
parts.note: the city's abbreviation NY sits inside both buNYan and tenNYson

explanation.surface: A city mentioned in the works of two English writers.
explanation.walkthrough: The city is not in their writing: its two-letter abbreviation sits inside both writers' names.
explanation.definitionFit: The great American city is routinely shortened to NY, the letters both surnames contain.

clue.text: Better information about art school for young kids

parts.note: kinder means nicer, better

indicators.note: about means going round something else

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Better information about an art school aimed at children.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery school or first year of schooling for small children.

clue.text: Online excellence could become a human right

parts.note: e- prefixes things done online, as in e-mail
excellence is high quality

explanation.surface: Excellence on the internet could one day be considered a human right.
explanation.definitionFit: Equal treatment of all people is enshrined among fundamental human rights.

clue.text: Wall builder heading off to become a pope

indicators.note: heading off says the first letter goes

parts.note: the Roman emperor Hadrian built the wall across northern England

explanation.surface: A wall builder sets off to become a pope.
explanation.definitionFit: Several popes took this name, including the only English pope, Adrian IV.

clue.text: Fighting greatened English decline

indicators.note: fighting suggests a scuffle, so the letters of greatened are thrown about

explanation.surface: Wars swelled England's power, then brought its decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'greatened' is a real but rare word, chosen because its letters fit.
explanation.definitionFit: To degenerate is to deteriorate, sink to a lower state: a verb synonym.

clue.text: Decrease in hostilities with a warmonger's capture

indicators.note: the phrase's capture is what it holds within it, the letters spanning its words

explanation.surface: Tensions ease after a warmonger is captured.
explanation.definitionFit: A thaw in relations is a figurative easing of tension, from melting ice.

clue.text: Great river polluted by drops of liquid ethyne? Just so

definitions.text: Great river polluted by drops of liquid ethyne? Just so

parts.note: ace means excellent, great

indicators.note: polluted by says letters get into the river's name

parts.note: the Tyne is a river in north-east England

indicators.note: drops of picks the first letters of liquid and ethyne

explanation.surface: A grand river fouled by spilled chemical: ethyne, as it happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just so' confirms the whole clue also describes the answer: ethyne is its chemical name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethyne is the systematic chemical name for the gas used in welding torches.

clue.text: Mud pie massaged into leg joint

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside another

parts.note: on is the leg side in cricket

indicators.note: massaged suggests kneading, so the letters of mud pie are worked around

explanation.surface: Mud pie massaged into a sore knee as a remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leg joint' reads as a knee or hip; 'leg' is ON (cricket's leg side) and 'joint', a dive or haunt, is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Joint is slang for a seedy establishment or haunt, like a den for smoking a narcotic.

clue.text: Slight setback when missing final beat in impromptu

indicators.note: setback says the piece is read backwards
missing final means the last letter goes

parts.note: slight means minor, unimportant
a pulse is a beat

explanation.surface: A small hiccup in an improvised performance when the last beat is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done impromptu is done spontaneously, without planning, on a whim.

clue.text: Hell is divine? Never

parts.note: to divine is to guess or deduce, to infer
no means not at all, never

explanation.surface: A theological question: could hell be divine? Never.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divine' looks like an adjective about the holy, but here it is a verb, to guess.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante's name for hell, borrowed from Italian, now used for any place of torment.

clue.text: Chicago girls hide in excited eagerness

indicators.note: the words hide the letters, which run across them

explanation.surface: Girls in Chicago hide, excited and eager.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog describes someone eagerly expectant, keen to see or hear more.

clue.text: Wake up girl hugging toppled tree

indicators.note: hugging means holding something else inside

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl

indicators.note: toppled suggests the letters of tree are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl hugging a fallen tree is told to wake up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toppled' is an anagram signal here rather than a reversal: the tree's letters fall into a new order inside the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are commands telling someone to face facts and see the true situation.

clue.text: Spray gel for fashionable travellers

parts.note: a jet is a spray of water
to gel is to set firm

explanation.surface: Hair spray and gel for stylish globetrotters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spray' and 'gel' look like hair products; here they are a squirt and a verb meaning to firm up.
explanation.definitionFit: The jet set are wealthy socialites who fly between fashionable places.

clue.text: A flood to join right-wing party in Israel (with wife)

indicators.note: in says the party goes inside the letters for Israel

parts.note: IL is the international code for Israel
the NF, National Front, is a British far-right party
ux is short for Latin uxor, wife, used in legal documents

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to join a nationalist party in Israel, bringing a spouse along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right-wing party in Israel' reads as Likud, but the party is Britain's National Front and Israel is its code IL. UX, for wife, is an old legal abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An influx is an inflow, a large arrival of people or things, like a flood.

clue.text: Foreign steersmen failing to complete university term

indicators.note: foreign suggests something strange, so the letters are rearranged
failing to complete says the last letter of the word is left off

explanation.surface: Overseas helmsmen don't finish their term of study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing to complete' drops the final N of 'steersmen'; 'Foreign' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Many universities divide the academic year into two halves, each a half-year teaching period.

clue.text: Drink starts to arrive in Downing Street

indicators.note: downing means swallowing, so those letters take another piece inside
starts to picks the first letters of arrive and in

explanation.surface: Drinks start to arrive at Downing Street, the British Prime Minister's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downing Street' reads as the address; 'Downing' means swallowing, so AI swallows ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine, named after its home town in Piedmont.

clue.text: Angry outbursts offering nothing to avoid asteroid crashing

indicators.note: crashing suggests a smash, so the remaining letters are scrambled
to avoid means leaving something out

parts.note: O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Angry rants about an asteroid that missed Earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to avoid' drops O from 'asteroid', and 'crashing' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Tirades are long, bitter speeches of denunciation, rants of fury.

clue.text: Headless American general buried in a European grave

indicators.note: buried in means set inside
headless says the first letter goes

parts.note: George Custer was the US general killed at Little Bighorn

explanation.surface: A beheaded American general lies buried in a European grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like a noun after 'European'; it is the adjective meaning solemn.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a stern, serious, unsmiling manner.

clue.text: Unintended interruption of octennial broadcast by detectives

indicators.note: interruption of says another piece breaks into the scrambled letters
broadcast means scattered, so the letters of octennial are spread anew

parts.note: the CID (Criminal Investigation Department) is the British police detective branch

explanation.surface: An eight-yearly broadcast is interrupted by police detectives, unintentionally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges OCTENNIAL to COINENTAL, which CID breaks into.
explanation.definitionFit: Something coincidental happens by chance, without being planned or meant.
